subject: Structured audit extract formats & legal-hold handoff
messages:
From: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com

Subject: RFP Q: audit exports & legal-hold handoff

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. As part of our compliance review we've got a couple of detailed asks on how Redwood would deliver audit data if we need to preserve logs for legal hold or e-discovery. Can you confirm the following at a high level and attach any manifest/spec examples?

1) Supported extract formats (JSONL, CSV, Parquet) and whether events are compressed and chunked by time-window.
2) Integrity & tamper evidence: do exports include signed checksums (SHA256) and a manifest file that lists file-level hashes and sequence ranges?
3) Delivery modes: S3 presigned URLs vs SCP vs encrypted streaming to our endpoint; are presigned URLs timebound and can they be vaulted to a KMS?
4) Retention windows and snapshotability: can we request point-in-time snapshots for arbitrary ranges up to retention limit?
5) Chain-of-custody notes: are there audit records of who exported the data and when?

We attached the RFP appendix with more context. Procurement may loop in for contract-level SLAs.

Appreciate a short technical write-up we can include with the RFP response.

Best,
Laura

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a small manifest spec and an export checklist we use for handoffs. Mara and Laura B. are looped for operational details and SLA language.

1) Formats & chunking: we support JSONL (primary), gzipped CSV, and Parquet exports on request. Exports are chunked by configurable time windows (default 1-hour chunks for high-volume tenants, configurable to daily). Each chunk is accompanied by a manifest .yaml/json describing sequence ranges and model/request metadata.

2) Integrity: every chunk file includes a SHA256 checksum. The manifest contains file-level hashes and an overall manifest hash. We optionally supply a manifest signed with our HSM-backed key to provide non-repudiation for legal processes.

3) Delivery modes: we support S3 presigned PUT/GET with configurable TTL, direct SFTP to customer endpoints, and encrypted streaming via mutual-TLS to a customer consumer URL. Presigned URLs can be generated under a customer-owned bucket and integrate with your KMS (we provide signed IAM policies if requested).

4) Snapshots & retention: point-in-time snapshots are available within configured retention windows. Hosted tenants default to 90 days; Dedicated/Private contracts can extend this (custom SLAs can go to 7 years with archival to cold storage). Snapshots are produced as read-only exports that capture KV caches and full event context for the selected range.

5) Chain-of-custody: export actions are recorded in our internal audit ledger: user, service account, timestamp, export parameters, and delivery confirmation. Ledger entries are immutable and included in the export package as an audit-activity.json file.

See attached: "redwood-audit-manifest-spec-v1.yaml" and an export handoff checklist. If you want we can produce a sample 24-hour export for a synthetic tenant for legal review.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Product Manager, Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-audit-manifest-spec-v1.yaml (yaml, 8KB)]

Laura — operational notes to complement Mina's technical write-up:

- We can produce exports on-demand (SLA: 48h for standard hosted customers, 8h for Dedicated with priority window).
- Export packaging: a .tar.gz per snapshot containing chunk files, manifest.json, audit-activity.json, and a signature file if requested.
- For legal-hold, we recommend an export delivered to your secured S3 with lifecycle disabled; alternatively we can hold an internal immutable archive for the contract duration and provide access logs.
- Cost: ad-hoc exports incur an extraction fee (covers egress and packaging). We'll provide a quote when we know size and retention term.

If Acme prefers, we can add a signed manifest step where our HSM signs the manifest and we provide verification tooling.

Marissa

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: RFP Q: audit exports & legal-hold handoff

Laura — attaching a sample manifest and a short verification README. Answers inline:

- Sample manifest fields: manifest_id, export_range_start, export_range_end, chunk_files (array of filenames with sha256), total_events, schema_version, produced_by (service/account), manifest_hash, signature_info (optional: signer_id, algorithm, cert_fingerprint). See attached YAML.
- Verification flow for HSM-signed manifests: we publish a verification public certificate bundle. The manifest signature is a PKCS#7 detached signature; verification is via `openssl cms -verify -in manifest.sig -content manifest.json -certfile redwood_pubchain.pem`. We will provide the pubchain and a short script for automation.
- Per-event encryption: for Dedicated and Private customers we support envelope encryption at export time using your CMK (we perform a data-key encryption step so exported chunks can only be decrypted with your key). For Hosted tenants we can arrange an S3 bucket owned by you with server-side encryption using your KMS CMK.

SLA / costs: standard hosted export SLA = 48h, extraction fee starts at $350 per TB extracted (estimates provided after scoping). Dedicated customers negotiate lower extraction fees in their contract.

I'll drop the two files to the Drive link and copy to the RFP bundle. If you want a POC export please let us know sample date range and preferred delivery.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Security Solutions
Redwood Inference
